title: AI adoption among US businesses

live.label: Ramp: all businesses paying for AI

sources.label: Ramp AI Index
Ramp AI adoption, overall (FRED RAMPAIALL)
U.S. Census Bureau, Business Trends and Outlook Survey (national estimates)

note: Ramp counts businesses with a card or invoice payment for AI; the Census BTOS lines (fortnightly, all employer firms) ask whether the business used AI in the last two weeks and expects to in the next six months.

title: US AI investment as a share of GDP

sources.label: Goldman Sachs Research: Global AI investment is forecast to exceed $1 trillion in 2026
sources.quote: Those estimates imply that AI capex will rise from 1.8% of GDP in the US (with global AI investment totaling 0.9% of global GDP) in 2026 to 2.5% of GDP in the US (1.3% globally) in 2027, with a further increase to 2.8% (1.4% globally) in 2028.

note: Goldman Sachs Research's extrapolation of its preferred estimates; it notes consensus 2027 capex projections are likely too conservative.

title: US AI-related investment, 2026

sources.label: Goldman Sachs Research: Global AI investment is forecast to exceed $1 trillion in 2026
sources.quote: That projection points to $1 trillion of AI-related investment around the globe in 2026, including $581 billion in the US

note: Investment (capex and related spending), not only software or subscription spend.

title: Worldwide AI infrastructure spending

sources.label: Gartner: Gartner Forecasts Worldwide AI Spending to Grow 49.5% in 2026
Gartner: Gartner Forecasts Worldwide AI Spending to Grow 47% in 2026 (May edition)

note: AI-optimized IaaS, servers, network fabric, AI processing semiconductors and devices; the largest segment of Gartner's AI spending forecast.

title: Hyperscaler cash capex (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle)

sources.label: FactSet Insight: Hyperscalers Tap External Financing as AI Capex Outruns Cash Flow
sources.quote: Aggregate cash capex of five hyperscalers is expected to exceed $690bn across their respective FY26 periods

note: Both figures are floors ("more than"), across each company's own fiscal year; FactSet's FY28 estimate is more than $900bn. Not a US-only total.

title: US AI spending, IDC 2028 forecast

sources.label: IDC via Business Wire: Worldwide Spending on AI Forecast to Reach $632 Billion in 2028
sources.quote: AI spending in the United States will reach $336 billion in 2028, making it the largest geographic region for AI investment

note: An August 2024 forecast (software, hardware and services; GenAI is $108B of it). Later Gartner and Goldman Sachs estimates are far higher.

title: Worldwide AI spending

sources.label: Gartner: Gartner Forecasts Worldwide AI Spending to Grow 49.5% in 2026
sources.quote: Total AI Spending 1,786,671 2,670,460 3,637,292 (millions of U.S. dollars, 2025, 2026, 2027)

sources.label: Yahoo Finance: AI spending to hit $2.53 trillion in 2026, $3.33 trillion in 2027 (Gartner, January forecast)
sources.quote: global AI spending will hit $2.53 trillion in 2026 and reach a staggering $3.33 trillion in 2027.

sources.label: Gartner: Gartner Forecasts Worldwide AI Spending to Grow 47% in 2026 (May edition)
sources.quote: Total AI Spending 1,764,947 2,595,667 3,493,358 (millions of U.S. dollars, 2025, 2026, 2027)

note: Gartner's September 2026 forecast, its third of the year: January and May editions (grey dotted) were both revised up. The 2025 value is Gartner's estimate.

title: AI's footprint on the US labour market

sources.label: Stanford HAI: Tracking AI's Real-Time Footprint on the Labor Market
Stanford Digital Economy Lab: AI Economic Indicators (monthly dashboards)

note: Stanford HAI reports employment in AI-exposed jobs down more than 4% this year, and for workers aged 22 to 25 in software development and customer service, employment down over 3% a year since ChatGPT's release, recently 4.4% (ADP payroll data; the authors call some findings preliminary).
